newsitem.title: CANADA: Maple Leaf sees greater pork exports.
newsitem.headline: Maple Leaf sees greater pork exports.

text.p: Canada's largest food processor expects to export a larger proportion of the pork it produces to the United States and Pacific Rim countries after it acquired Burns Foods meat operations on Monday, Maple Leaf Foods Inc's chief executive told Reuters.

"One out of three pigs we slaughter gets exported and I frankly think that the day will come in the near future where it's one out of two. There'll be significant opportunities," Maple Leaf chief executive Archie McLean, told Reuters.
Maple Leaf bought Burns' hog and beef slaughter plants in Manitoba and Alberta and its Saskatchewan bacon plant Monday.
The sum of the purchase was not disclosed.
Maple Leaf distributes its products in western Canada despite not having any processing facilities there while Burns sold product in eastern Canada without having an industrial presence there.
The acquisition should reduce distribution costs, add to domestic market share as well as export market share, McLean said.
"Burns has some significant sales in the United States presently in certain regions and we think we can build on that," McLean said.
